record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: What is the chromatic number of the graph on the Euclidean plane in which two points are adjacent exactly when their Euclidean distance is an odd integer?

evidence.quote: For A ⊆ R, let GA (En ) be the graph in En with vertex set En and edge set {x, y ∈ En : kx − yk ∈ A}. Very recently Ardal, Maňuch, Rosenfeld, Shelah and Stacho have shown in [1] that if we let X be the set of all odd integers, then χ(GX (E2 )) ≥ 5, but the current upper bound on this number is the trivial bound ℵ0 .

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the graph $G$ whose vertex set is the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, in which two distinct points $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^2$ are joined by an edge if and only if their Euclidean distance $\|x - y\|$ is an odd positive integer. Determine the chromatic number $\chi(G)$, i.e., the least cardinal $\kappa$ such that there exists a function $c : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \kappa$ with $c(x) \neq c(y)$ whenever $\|x - y\|$ is an odd integer.
artifact.category_tag: Euclidean Ramsey theory / chromatic number of distance graphs
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Davies, "Odd Distances in Colourings of the Plane", GAFA 2024) proved that every finite colouring of the plane contains a monochromatic pair of points at odd integer distance. Combined with the known existence of countable colourings of the odd-distance graph, this establishes that the chromatic number of the odd-distance graph in the plane equals $\aleph_0$, resolving Rosenfeld's problem.

status_evidence.title: Odd Distances in Colourings of the Plane | GAFA
status_evidence.snippet: Every finite colouring of the plane contains a monochromatic pair of points at an odd distance from each other. Since there are countable colourings of the odd distance graph, the chromatic number of the odd distance graph is countably infinite, solving Rosenfeld's odd distance problem.
status_evidence.claim: The chromatic number of the odd-distance plane graph is $\aleph_0$, resolving the problem.

status_evidence.title: Coloring the Odd Distance Graph | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: Problem of determining the chromatic number of the graph on R^2 where two points are adjacent if their distance is an odd integer, posed by Rosenfeld.
